subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. ACME.ai & OmniServe
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@pulsehealth.com>, Mike Ong <mike.ong@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. ACME.ai & OmniServe

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the candid discussion. Per our call, below is a short recap of what we heard, the decision criteria you highlighted, open questions, and proposed next steps. Let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you confirmed
- Production latency variability on short-tail queries (customer-facing chat) during peak traffic.
- High cost per 100k requests with current vendor due to low cache hit-rate and lack of batching options.
- Difficulty getting deterministic rollout testing (canary) across regions.

Goals for the bake-off
1) Meet 95th percentile latency target <= 120ms for 1-2 token responses at 200 RPS/region.
2) Demonstrate 30-40% reduction in per-token CPU/GPU cost through batching + prefix caching.
3) Show a reproducible canary/rollback workflow and audit logs for compliance.

Decision criteria (what your committee will weigh)
- Latency under realistic load (p50/p95),
- Unit cost per token at scale,
- Ease of integration (API, SDKs),
- Security/compliance artifacts (SOC2, retention controls),
- Support & SLAs, especially for multi-region failover.

Open questions we captured
- What’s the expected end-to-end latency with KV/prefix caching disabled? (you want worst-case numbers)
- Can Redwood produce per-token cost breakdown by route (chat vs. embeddings)?
- What would a canary rollback look like across us-west/us-east?

Follow-up tests Redwood proposed
- Baseline run (no caching, 200 RPS, 1-2 token responses) to measure worst-case latency.
- Cache-enabled run (same load) to measure hit-rate effect.
- Batch/throughput run to measure unit-cost improvements at 1k and 5k RPS.
- Canary simulation: scripted rollouts + rollback across regions.

Next steps / ownership
- Redwood to run baseline + cache-enabled runs and provide perf logs and a bake-off matrix (Marissa, Aditya).
- PulseHealth to provide synthetic traffic profile and access to a small dev dataset with PII stripped for parity (Sarah/Mike).
- Follow-up call w/ results and vendor comparison in one week — proposed Thu 11/5 10am PT.

Attachments: PulseHealth_bakeoff_matrix.xlsx (template)

Thanks — I’ll start the test runs tomorrow and share logs as soon as the baseline finishes.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

---

From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@pulsehealth.com>

Cc: Mike Ong <mike.ong@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. ACME.ai & OmniServe

Marissa — thanks for the recap, this looks right to me. Quick clarifications: 

1) For the baseline run, the team specifically wants the "cache disabled" numbers since that's been our pain point in production — can you include latency percentiles for both short (1-2 token) and medium (16-32 token) responses?

2) Regarding cost breakdown, can you show the per-route (chat vs. embeddings) cost and an assumed traffic mix (our current is ~80% chat, 20% embeddings)?

3) Also: can you confirm whether Redwood supports audit logs with at least 90 days retention out-of-the-box or if that’s an add-on? Compliance is a gating item.

We can share the sanitized dev dataset by EOD today and the synthetic traffic script early tomorrow. 11/5 10am PT works for the follow-up call.

On a separate note — ACME.ai said they can run the 5k RPS test but did not provide worst-case latency numbers yet. Would be great to have your worst-case numbers for parity.

Thanks,
Sarah
Director, Product Infrastructure
PulseHealth

Thanks Sarah — confirmed. Answers inline below and next steps.

- Latency percentiles: we will provide p50/p90/p95 for both 1-2 token and 16-32 token responses in the baseline. Baseline run will have caching disabled to capture worst-case numbers.

- Cost breakdown: we will produce a per-route cost table using your 80/20 chat/embeddings mix plus a sensitivity run at 70/30. This will be in the bake-off matrix.

- Audit logs: Redwood provides audit logs and basic retention to 90 days in our standard enterprise tier; long-term retention is available as an add-on. We'll include the SOC2 report and retention options in the packet.

Attached: redwood_perf_logs_q3.zip (sample logs from recent runs) - raw perf dumps and the run scripts we will use.

Action items (owners):
- Aditya: run baseline (cache disabled) + 1k/5k batch runs by EOD 11/4. Share perf logs to this thread and upload to the shared Drive folder.
- Marcus: prepare canary rollout plan + scripted rollback example for us-west -> us-east by 11/5 call.
- Marissa (me): consolidate bake-off matrix and vendor comparison slide for the 11/5 call.

Proposed follow-up: Thu 11/5 10am PT - 45 min to review results and next steps. Dial-in + shared Drive link to follow.

Best,
Marissa
